categories.summary: Saudi Arabia intercepted two Houthi missiles overnight and debris fell in the Mecca region (the Houthis deny targeting Mecca). Iran still says Hormuz stays shut until its demands are met; no new US or Iranian strikes confirmed. Taiwan reports a second Chinese naval combat patrol in a week and 'area denial' drills in the Western Pacific - pressure, not a blockade.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command aircraft (3 E-6s seen) and tanker activity are normal; no private-jet movement to retreat destinations. Forecast-market nuclear-test odds are under 3%. The lit 'mobilisation' sign is a Russian recruitment story, not a call-up.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: All Australian carriers are normal (largest drop 4.8% on a tiny Vodafone sample), the SA grid is normal with no reserve warnings and the global threat level is green. CISA added several exploited Barracuda, Cisco and Outlook flaws this week; Australian ransomware listings are below normal. The ACSC feed timed out this run.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological

sources.title: Nature World News: Ebola cases top 10,000 in Congo

categories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continues in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria (reports say more than 10,000 cases in Congo), with no cases outside Africa. The lit 'chemical attack' and 'unexplained deaths' signs are false matches (a Syria trials article and a fitness story).

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges and no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or Bureau severe-weather warnings. Six small incidents across SA (grass and structure fires, a burn-off). A strong wind warning covers Spencer Gulf for 14 November and several outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding.

categories.summary: Hormuz traffic is still only about 4 ships a day (versus 100+ before the war). Brent rose 1.9% to US$94.50 and the Australian dollar fell 0.9% to 68 US cents, so SA fuel prices are likely to stay high or rise. Malacca, Lombok and Sunda routes into Australia are normal.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Brent US$94.50 (+1.9%), VIX 17.5 (flat), gold US$3,881 (-3.0%), AUD 0.681 (-0.9%). Markets calm overall; the weaker dollar and firmer oil are the main cost pressures for SA households.

headline: Watch: the Iran-Hormuz standoff continues and Houthi missiles were intercepted near Mecca, keeping fuel the main risk for SA; nothing locally.
summary: Saudi Arabia intercepted two Houthi missiles overnight with debris falling in the Mecca region, and Iran still says Hormuz stays shut until its demands are met; no new US or Iranian strikes are confirmed. Brent rose about 2% to US$94.50 while the Australian dollar fell to 68 US cents, so SA fuel prices are likely to stay high. Yesterday's Gulf GPS-jamming flag fits the ongoing missile activity, not a new attack. Locally: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no bans or warnings, grid and phone networks normal.
